title: Penalty Points, New Drivers & Disqualification
whatItIs: Courts endorse a driving record with penalty points (1 to 11 per offence). Too many points means a ban, and new drivers face a lower limit for 2 years after their first test.

keyFacts.text: A driver with 12 or more points within 3 years MUST be disqualified, for at least 6 months.
For dangerous driving and drink-driving the court MUST disqualify: at least 12 months.

keyFacts: New drivers: 6 or more points within 2 years of passing the first test and the licence is revoked.
Unexpired points on a provisional licence carry over and count towards the new driver's 6.
Endorsements stay on the record for 4 years, or 11 years for drink or drug driving.

visual.caption: The numbers that lead to a ban

items.label: Within 2 years of passing: licence revoked
Ban this long or more: apply for a new licence

b.label: New drivers (first 2 years)
points: 6 or more points, including points carried over
Licence revoked: new provisional, then theory and practical tests again

onTheTest.question: A pupil passed 18 months ago with 3 unexpired points from their provisional licence. They now get 3 more. What happens?
options: They must take an extended test only
Their licence is revoked; they must pass theory and practical tests again
onTheTest.why: Unexpired provisional points carry over. 6 or more points within 2 years of passing means the licence is cancelled; they need a new provisional licence and must pass both tests again.

onTheTest.question: What is the minimum disqualification for a second drink-drive offence within 10 years?
onTheTest.why: Highway Code annex 5: a second drink-drive offence in the space of 10 years results in a minimum of 3 years' disqualification.

traps: The new driver rule applies even if the offences were paid by fixed penalty.
Passing a test for another category (e.g. a lorry) does not start a new 2-year period.
Every offence with points also gives the court a discretionary power to disqualify.
Totting-up ban: 6 months; 12 months if it is a second ban within 3 years; 2 years if a third.
